summary: Pema Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Shenphen Nangwa. He served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn, attested in 1982.
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Penghao Sun is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He completed doctoral studies under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under teachers including Mark Elliott, Peter K. Bol, Weirong Shen, and Qingying Chen (2009–2011).
Penor 02 studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught both Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Palyul Monastery under teachers including Thubten Chökyi Dawa and Karma Tekchok Nyingpo. He founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978 and taught numerous students.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1934–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Copenhagen under Erik Haarh. He was a lecturer at Copenhagen (1982–1989) and professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

Per Kværne (born 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Oslo under Nils Simonsson. He held posts at the University of Bergen and the University of Oslo.

Peri Bhaskararao (1947–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He was Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1973–1998) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1998–2011).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1966–1971) and held a post at the University of Marburg (~1971–1991).

Perry Link (born 1944) is a Sinologist who completed his B.A. at Harvard (~1962–1966). He held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

Peter Adamson (born 1972) is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Williams College and the University of Notre Dame. He held posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).

Peter Alan Roberts works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied with traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed doctoral research under Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop (born 1972) is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Groningen under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He was a lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and an editor at Leiden University.
Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and became a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock (born 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies and studied at Yale University. He served as Asian Studies Development Program Coordinator at the East-West Center and held an affiliated post at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy and held a post at Deakin University. He studied under advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, as well as traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.
